name: Credentials in AD Object Properties — Discovery & Detection
description: Admins sometimes store passwords in AD user object Description or Info fields, incorrectly assuming these fields require elevated privileges to read. Every domain user can read most object properties. Detection: baseline user behavior and alert on 4624/4625/4768 from unexpected sources for the affected account.
notes:
=== BACKGROUND ===
  Every domain user can read most AD object properties by default
  Description and Info fields are fully readable by all authenticated users
  Common admin mistake: storing temp passwords or service account passwords in Description

=== ATTACK: PowerShell Function ===
# Load the search function (paste into PS session)
Function SearchUserClearTextInformation {
    Param (
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][Array] $Terms,
        [Parameter(Mandatory=$false)][String] $Domain
    )
    if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($Domain)) {
        $dc = (Get-ADDomain).RIDMaster
    } else {
        $dc = (Get-ADDomain $Domain).RIDMaster
    }
    $list = @()
    foreach ($t in $Terms) {
        $list += "(`$_.Description -like `"*$t*`")"
        $list += "(`$_.Info -like `"*$t*`")"
    }
    Get-ADUser -Filter * -Server $dc -Properties Enabled,Description,Info,PasswordNeverExpires,PasswordLastSet |
        Where { Invoke-Expression ($list -join ' -OR ') } |
        Select SamAccountName,Enabled,Description,Info,PasswordNeverExpires,PasswordLastSet |
        fl
}

# Run it: search for 'pass' in Description/Info fields
SearchUserClearTextInformation -Terms "pass"

# Multiple terms
SearchUserClearTextInformation -Terms "pass","pw","secret","key"

# Target specific domain
SearchUserClearTextInformation -Terms "pass" -Domain "<DOMAIN>"

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4738: 'A user account was changed'
  → Does NOT show which property changed or new values
  → Can detect when non-admin modifies a user object (naming convention violation)
  → Alert if non-privileged user modifies any user account

Event 4624/4625 (logon success/failure) and 4768 (Kerberos TGT):
  → Correlate against expected logon locations for the account
  → Service accounts authenticating from workstations = suspicious

Honeypot technique:
  → Create service account with fake password in Description field
  → Account is enabled, has old password (2+ years), has logins
  → Any 4625/4771/4776 for this account = alert

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Continuous assessments to detect credentials in object properties
  → Educate admins: never put passwords in Description/Info
  → Automate user creation to minimize manual admin handling
